propositions: Nested pytest children that execute without explicit --basetemp allocate from the user-global numbered temp root and trigger cleanup of unrelated trees at session finish.

tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py::test_engine_submodules_resolve_when_the_tests_unit_shadow_is_active launches a mixed-module child pytest without parent-owned basetemp, causing it to delete cleanup-eligible sentinel files in the shared numbered root.

tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py::test_repro_module_passes_standalone launches a standalone pytest child without parent-owned basetemp, causing it to delete cleanup-eligible sentinel files in the shared numbered root.

Pytest 9.1.1 TempPathFactory.getbasetemp creates and registers cleanup for the numbered root, while pytest_sessionfinish only skips cleanup when _basetemp is None, making executing children vulnerable.

Safe nested pytest launchers in tests/_store_isolation.py, tests/unit/test_external_isolation.py, and tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py pass tmp_path-derived --basetemp to their children, establishing the parent-owned isolation pattern.
Repair requires assigning each executing nested child a unique tmp_path-derived --basetemp and verifying the child materializes that assigned directory.
